name: Treaty with the Miami (Eel River or Thorntown party), 1828
promises: Article 2: besides $2,000 in goods already delivered, the United States would pay $8,000 in goods, build twelve log houses, clear and fence forty acres on the five mile reservation on Eel River, and supply a wagon, two yoke of oxen, two hands to work three months a year for two years, $500 of provisions, and five horses with saddles and bridles.
Article 3: the United States would pay Peter Langlois $1,000 in silver and $3,000 in goods for the party's debts.
Article 4: the United States would set aside $1,000 a year for five years for the education of Miami youth; the President and Senate could strike this article.

breaches.what: The Miami Tribe of Oklahoma and the Miami Indians of Indiana claimed additional compensation for the Thorntown Reservation ceded by this treaty. The claim was never tried; the Commission approved a settlement of $66,966 after consideration and offsets.
breaches.whoFoundIt: Indian Claims Commission, Dockets 255 and 124-C, 20 Ind. Cl. Comm. 97

source.title: Miami Tribe of Oklahoma et al. v. United States, Dockets 255 and 124-C, Findings of Fact on Compromise Settlement (December 3, 1968)
source.publisher: Indian Claims Commission decisions, Oklahoma State University Library

landTaken: The Commission records that the Thorntown Reservation, described as ten miles square, contained 64,037.87 acres.
compensation: The Commission records a treaty consideration of $19,485.00 and approved a settlement of $66,966 in 1968.
today: The settlement made no finding that the 1828 price was unconscionable.

openQuestions: The Miami Tribe of Oklahoma's own account of the Thorntown cession was not located.
The Miami Indians of Indiana are not federally recognized; they are named because they were a petitioner.

Audit 2026-11-08: Article 2 promise reworded to match the treaty text (two hands for three months in each year for two years, not two hired hands for two years; the $2,000 in goods already delivered and the $500 of provisions added).

plain.promised: The Eel River Miami gave up their Thorntown reservation for goods, houses, cleared land, livestock and an education fund, and moved to their Eel River reservation.
plain.happened: The Miami sued for more payment. The claim was settled before the Claims Commission decided whether the price was fair.
plain.today: The Commission approved a $66,966 settlement in 1968.
